svg.title: CERF C-Max HUD · adaptive layouts and gearshift concepts
svg.desc: Three responsive HUD studies: a wide desktop with side rails, a compact desktop with an essential bottom strip, and a portrait screen with stacked audio, climate, and gear controls. Three proposed PRNDL gear selectors compare a lever rail, large touch segments, and a compact popover. Guest display aspect ratio stays 800 by 480. Selected and pending gears are shown distinctly.
svg.text: CERF / FORD SYNC 2 / C-MAX HUD STUDY 02
A console that fits the window
Side rails for wide screens. A small strip for tight windows. The familiar stack for portrait.
Use horizontal space for controls; the guest display and essential buttons fit together.
Stack the console below the guest display.
Essential controls fit before secondary details
Keep the C-Max audio / climate grouping.
Use spare height for the gear selector.
Secondary details may scroll below the controls.
Fit the screen first; keep a single essential strip, with secondary controls one click away.
Scaled to fit · aspect ratio preserved
remain available in the Car panel.
Switch by available width AND height.
Three presentations of the same proposed input. The active gear follows guest-confirmed state.
Best when there is spare horizontal space.
Drag snaps to discrete positions on release.
Focused keys can select a gear directly.
Tap another position to request it.
Large, equal touch targets; no dragging needed.
Keep selected gear visibly marked with text
and an outline, as well as the accent color.
Show the selected gear in a compact pill.
Open all positions only when requested.
Close on selection, Escape, or outside click.
A gear request gets a pending marker; the selected gear changes after guest confirmation.
Layout follows available window space, not platform alone. Gearshift and climate UI shown here are concepts for future wiring.
